e.g. $I$ hope to see you in office tomorrow.

Why? Do you want to discuss anything in particular?

Yes. We're trying to set up a new office in town.

We intend to make it bigger than the present one.

We've managed to buy a good plot and expect to finish the legal formalities soon. We've already arranged to appoint an internationally reputed architect.

I wish to make it look unique. I've failed to make some of my dreams come true, but this time I plan not to fail.

We also use the **to infinitive** after some verbs connected with thinking, such as *decide*, *forget*, *remember*, etc.

e.g. I've decided to do some part-time job during the summer holidays. And although I remembered to discuss it with my best friend in school, I forgot to tell my parents about it.

We use the **to infinitive** after some verbs connected with saying that we will or will not do something, such as *agree*, *refuse*, *offer*, *promise*, etc.

e.g. Rahela had agreed to sell her computer at half price to me, but refused to do so at the last moment. I offered to give a slightly higher price, and she accepted that. I promised not to make any more deals with her.

The negative form is **not + to infinitive**:

e.g. Remember not to drive too fast.

I've decided not to accept the offer.
